turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please come in. Is someone with you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): My husband is sitting outside. I told him not to bother, it's a small thing only.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): We can call him later if we need to. What brought you in?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): The home test was positive. There's a little discomfort, nothing much. I almost cancelled.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any idea how many weeks you might be?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The last period was around Diwali, or after. I didn't note the date. Maybe eight weeks, maybe ten, I honestly can't say.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any bleeding since that period?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No bleeding. Everyone panics for no reason.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And pain in the tummy?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Pain? Um, no, not really.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about nausea, vomiting, fever, or giddiness?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): The date is the messy part. Diwali week we were at my parents' and then I travelled, and I lost track of...
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry. A little queasy in the mornings, once or twice. No fever. I didn't feel giddy.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): This discomfort you mentioned, where exactly is it?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Low, in the centre. It comes and goes. Very mild, I was on my work calls as usual.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it a cramp, the way a period feels?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes. A little crampy, like a period but lighter. I shouldn't have said there was no pain.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when has that cramp been there?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe four or five days. Or from last week. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any burning when you pass urine? Any unusual discharge?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No burning. Urine is normal. No funny discharge also.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which medicines are you on now?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid in the morning, and thyroxine. The folic acid is...
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, I cut across. What strength of folic acid?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Five milligram, one tablet. Thyroxine I think is fifty microgram, but don't quote me on that.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long on the thyroxine, and why was it started?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Since last winter, or the one before. TSH was high, underactive thyroid. The paper is at home.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any operation in the past? And in the family, diabetes, blood pressure, pregnancy losses?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation. My mother has diabetes. I haven't heard of miscarriages in the family. This is my first pregnancy.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing at all.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or take alcohol?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. We stay in Koramangala, just the two of us. I work from home in software. The deadlines are mad, but that's not why I'm here.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): A few things are still unclear, the dates especially. May I call your husband in?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): If you have to. He worries more than I do. Just don't let him make a scene.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please come in. We'll keep it to the facts.
[SEG0037] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, I was waiting outside only. She didn't want me to come, but she's been very tense since that test.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): She's told me about the positive test, a lower cramp, folic acid and thyroxine. I still need bleeding clarified.
[SEG0039] person_3 (CAREGIVER): There was spotting. She showed me the pad, brown, not a proper flow.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): That was a stain. Hardly anything. I said no because it isn't real bleeding.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): So there has been some spotting?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes. A little brown spotting. Not red, and it didn't soak a pad. I didn't want a fuss.
[SEG0043] person_3 (CAREGIVER): It wasn't yesterday only. She told me about it three days back.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it was yesterday. Or maybe the day before. You're adding days, it was not three.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll take the spotting as roughly one to three days, without a fixed start. You remember it differently.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She vomited also. Two times this morning, in the bathroom.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I did not vomit. I was queasy and I spat in the sink. That is not vomiting. Don't add things.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll keep that as a disagreement. You describe queasiness, he describes two vomits.
[SEG0049] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And the folic acid, she misses doses. She says later, and the tablet is still sitting in the strip.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it most days. I missed one or two, that's all. I have not stopped it.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): So daily use is uncertain. On the thyroxine, she thought fifty microgram.
[SEG0052] person_3 (CAREGIVER): The strip at home is twenty-five microgram. One tablet every morning. I give it to her.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): I think they increased it to fifty. He might be looking at an old strip. I can't sort it today.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then the dose stays unclear. Keep taking it for the thyroid, bring the current strip, and don't change it yourself.
[SEG0055] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Years ago a sulphur tablet gave her an itchy rash, all over the body.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): It did not. I have no allergies. That was a heat rash, and I don't remember any tablet. Old stories.
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll note a possible sulpha rash that the two of you dispute, and we'll avoid sulpha drugs.
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is eighty-eight, and blood pressure is one-ten over seventy-two. Temperature is thirty-six point six. Oxygen saturation is ninety-nine percent.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): The abdomen is soft. There is mild tenderness low in the centre. No guarding and no rebound. I'll leave the internal check till after the scan.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): See, mild only. So I can go home after this, isn't it?
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not yet. I want an early pregnancy scan today, and blood tests today, haemoglobin, blood group, and serum beta-hCG.
[SEG0062] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Can they do all of that here, today itself?
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. I'm placing both requests now. The scan goes to radiology, the bloods to the lab.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): You're making it sound bigger than it is. A little stain, a little cramp. That's all this is.

[SEG0065] person_1 (DOCTOR): I understand that you want to minimise it. This impression is provisional only: it may be a threatened miscarriage, and it could also be harmless spotting in early pregnancy. The scan has to separate those.
[SEG0066] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Should we start a medicine? Does she need to stay in bed the whole day?

[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rest at home. No heavy lifting, and no intercourse until we know more. Continue folic acid five milligram every morning, and try not to skip it. I am not starting progesterone today.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): If the cramp comes, then what?
[SEG0069] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll write paracetamol, five hundred milligram, one tablet up to three times a day after food, when the cramp is there. Do not take ibuprofen or Meftal.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. I also had a urine infection last winter, or the one before. I finished whatever antibiotic they gave. Probably useless to mention.
[SEG0071] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Her sleep is poor. She's up half the night worrying, ever since the test was positive.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm sleeping. A little less, maybe. And I'm not anxious. It's just... anyway.

[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back so we agree. Home test positive, last period around Diwali or after with no firm date, brown spotting about one to three days, and mild cramps for several days with an unclear onset. Morning queasiness is noted, vomiting is not agreed, folic acid is five milligram with some misses, the thyroxine dose is not agreed, and an old sulpha rash is disputed. No fever, no burning urine, no giddiness, pulse eighty-eight, pressure one-ten over seventy-two, and the tummy is soft with mild central tenderness.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you for not writing a fixed week. I only said Diwali, or after. I do not know.
[SEG0075] person_1 (DOCTOR): Once the scan and the bloods are done, come back to me later today and we will read them together.
[SEG0076] person_3 (CAREGIVER): What if it gets worse before we are back?

[SEG0077] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the bleeding becomes heavy, or you soak a pad within an hour, or the pain becomes severe, or you feel faint, or you get shoulder pain, come straight to emergency. Don't sit at home waiting.
[SEG0078] person_2 (PATIENT): Emergency still feels like too much. If it truly gets worse, I'll come. I still think it is nothing.
[SEG0079] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll bring her later today. I'll also carry the thyroxine strip so you can see the dose.
[SEG0080] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Reception will book the scan and the blood tests now. We meet again when the reports are in hand.
[SEG0081] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Let's do the scan and finish, then.
[SEG0082] person_1 (DOCTOR): One last thing. If those warning signs show up, it is the emergency department, not a wait until evening.

spec.situation: Woman about 8-10 weeks pregnant with spotting and cramps; unsure of dates ('the last period was around Diwali, or after'); anxious; partner waits outside then joins. Scan and blood tests planned today, strict return advice.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

omissions.text: Estimated gestation was discussed as uncertain, with the patient saying she might be about 8 to 10 weeks pregnant but could not say for sure.

Abdominal pain was initially denied and then corrected by the patient: she said the discomfort was low central, intermittent, very mild, crampy like a lighter period, and that she 'shouldn't have said there was no pain.'
Nausea was asked together with vomiting and the patient reported only being a little queasy in the mornings once or twice; vomiting remained disputed rather than confirmed by the patient.
This is the patient's first pregnancy.
The patient denied family history of miscarriages/pregnancy losses.
The patient reported no pain 'not really' before later clarifying mild crampy pain, so the initial denial/correction was part of the history.
Internal/pelvic examination was deferred until after the scan.
Doctor explicitly advised to keep taking thyroxine for the thyroid and not to change the dose herself until the current strip is reviewed.
Doctor explicitly decided not to start progesterone today.
Paracetamol was to be taken after food when cramping occurs.

Return precautions were specifically to go straight to the emergency department, not wait at home or until evening, if bleeding became heavy, a pad was soaked within an hour, pain became severe, faintness occurred, or shoulder pain developed.
Follow-up was specifically to come back later the same day after the scan and blood tests so the doctor could review the results together.
